analysis: The closest option retains the molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, lab and physiology spine. Evolution supplies direct gene-to-population depth and ecology adds organism-environment mechanisms. Numerical methods give an explicit mathematical modeling contribution. The medicine option retains the molecular, drug and disease spine and extends it through epidemiology, health psychology, developmental trajectories, ethical reasoning and research synthesis. The quantitative plan shifts academic weight to linear algebra, linear systems, programming, neural networks and imaging. It is a quantitative life-science option with transferable tools, with no claim of dedicated biological physics or structural-biology methods. The broad and quantitative plans share meaningful life science and data preparation but differ on evolutionary and organismal breadth versus signals and numerical analysis. The curriculum leaves organic drug synthesis, physical chemistry, biological physics and structural methods visible as gaps. Optional independent research sits outside the UCR 180 EC.

alignment.rationale: Both study cell organization, membranes and molecular processes.
Both examine biomolecules and the chemistry of living systems.
Both study how organisms function. UCR concentrates on human physiology.
Utrecht studies organic chemistry of drug molecules. UCR Pharmacology covers related drug action and disposition.
Both develop practical molecular and biochemical laboratory skills.
Both develop statistical reasoning. Utrecht also integrates academic writing in this course.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC research project. UCR independent research is optional and outside the scheduled degree.
Both develop mathematics for quantitative life science. UCR teaches programming in a separate course.
Utrecht provides dedicated physical chemistry and spectroscopy.
Utrecht applies physical principles directly to biological systems. UCR provides related mathematics and biology.
Utrecht teaches structural biology and biophysical laboratory methods as a dedicated course.
Utrecht includes 45 EC of free electives.
Utrecht requires six major electives. Its four advisory profiles help students choose their own combination.
